blocks.text: The standard hydrogen electrode is one of several types of half-cell that can be used as reference electrode. Figure 10.4 shows a standard hydrogen electrode.

items: Hydrogen gas at 101 kPa pressure, in equilibrium with H⁺ ions of concentration 1.00 mol dm⁻³
A platinum electrode covered with platinum black in contact with the hydrogen gas and the H⁺ ions.

blocks.text: The platinum black is finely divided platinum, which allows close contact of hydrogen gas and H⁺ ions in solution so that equilibrium between H₂ gas and H⁺ ions is established quickly. The platinum electrode is inert so it does not take part in the reaction. Standard electrode potential E° values for all half-cells are measured relative to this electrode.

blocks.alt: Standard hydrogen electrode. A glass tube with a side inlet labelled Hydrogen gas supply at 1 atm pressure stands in a beaker of solution labelled H+ (1 mol/dm3). A platinum wire runs down the tube to a black platinum electrode. The tube widens at the bottom into a glass 'bell' with a hole in for H2 to bubble out; bubbles rise beside it.

blocks.text: The printed Figure 10.4 gives the acid concentration as ‘1mol/dm⁺³’; it is 1 mol/dm³ (1.00 mol dm⁻³), as drawn above.
